## Modern Web Guidance (Source)
This repo is the source repository for GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents.

Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform.

See CONTRIBUTING.md and GOVERNANCE.md for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase.

---

Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.

Documentation · Eval Dashboard · Source Code · Report an Issue
## Quickstart
This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See Alternative Installation Methods below.
## Why?
Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions.

Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code.

Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap. Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on:
 Modern Browser APIs: Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse.
 Performance & Accessibility: Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances.
 Responsible Fallbacks: Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries.
## What's Included?
We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are designed to be token-efficient; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know.

row.description: Use your most capable model to audit your codebase and write plans for cheaper models to execute.

markdown:
## improve
An agent skill that audits any codebase and writes implementation plans for other agents to execute.

The idea: use your most capable model for the part where intelligence compounds — understanding the codebase, judging what's worth doing, writing the spec — and hand execution to cheaper models. The skill never implements anything itself. The plan is the product.
## Install
Works in any agent that supports Agent Skills format. The plans it writes are plain markdown, so any agent (or human) can pick them up.
## How to use
A typical first run, start to finish:

1. Open your agent in the repo and run /improve (or /improve quick to keep it cheap).
2. It maps the repo, audits it, and comes back with a findings table. Reply with the ones you want planned — "plan 1, 3 and 5".
3. Plans land in plans/ — one file each, plus an index with the recommended order. Read them; they're meant to be reviewed.
4. Hand a plan to any agent ("implement plans/001-.md"), or let the skill run it: /improve execute 001. It dispatches a cheaper model in an isolated worktree, reviews the diff against the plan, and reports back with a verdict. Merging stays up to you.
5. Next session, run /improve reconcile to clean up the backlog: verify what landed, refresh what drifted, unblock what got stuck.

Before a PR, /improve branch does the same thing scoped to just what your branch changes.
## Example
A run against shadcn/ui came back with findings like:



…and rejected a few, with reasons recorded so they don't come back next run:



Picking #1 produced this plan — current code excerpted, exact steps, the repo's own test/lint commands as verification gates, and STOP conditions for when reality doesn't match.

## Codex Security
Codex Security helps you find, investigate, and fix vulnerabilities in your code.
Use its security workflows in Codex, or automate them with the
@openai/codex-security CLI and TypeScript SDK.

- In Codex: choose a security workflow.
- In a terminal: install the CLI and scan your repository.
- In automation: use the TypeScript SDK or
 GitHub Action.
## Features
- Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes. Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return their deduplicated findings.
- Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes.
- Draft SECURITY.md policies and save threat models for later review.
- Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against
 your own rubric, and suggest owners from source and Git history.
- Preview third-party scanner findings, save them locally, or publish supported reports to Codex Security Cloud. Scanner import guides.
- Track findings in Linear, Jira, or GitHub, publish completed scans, or export SARIF, JSON, and CSV. Integration workflows.
- Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and
 containers.
## Use in Codex
Open your repository in a Codex session with the Codex Security plugin enabled,
then ask:

> Run a Codex Security scan on this repository, focusing on authentication and
> authorization. Return the saved report, source evidence, and coverage limits.

A completed scan saves a report and findings. Read the report for source
evidence and exclusions, then request a patch or ask Codex to verify an
existing fix. See the agent workflow guide for setup,
task selection, and recovery.
## Quick start
Requires Node.js 22.13.0+ within 22.x, or Node.js 24.x or 26.x, and Python 3.10+.
Python 3.10 also requires tomli.

Install the CLI globally and sign in:



Run your first scan from the repository directory:



When the scan completes, open the Markdown file at the REPORT path in the
terminal. Run cs scans show from the same repository to find its latest
completed scan again. See scan scope and follow-up work
for how to interpret exclusions in the report.

cs and codex-security run the same CLI. If the short name conflicts with
another command, use codex-security. To skip the global install, or if npm
reports an EEXIST conflict, use npx @openai/codex-security in place of
cs for both login and scanning.

For CI, set OPENAIAPIKEY or CODEXAPIKEY in the scan process's environment.
For a headless machine, see device or SSH login.

linkedDocuments.markdown:
## Security workflows in Codex
Use Codex Security to scan code, investigate a supplied finding, or make and
verify a security fix. Choose the task that matches the evidence you already
have; a repository scan is the default when you are looking for new findings.
## Get started
Open your repository in Codex. Find Codex Security in the desktop plugin
browser, or enter /plugins in the interactive Codex CLI. Install the plugin,
confirm it is enabled, and start a new chat. See the
plugin quickstart for host setup
and access requirements.

Ask for the task in plain language, including the repository or paths and any
security context:

> Scan this repository with Codex Security. Focus on authorization boundaries,
> use the existing SECURITY.md, and return the saved report and coverage limits.

The task map below also gives explicit skill names. Local scans
do not require the optional Cloud connection. To read existing Cloud findings,
follow the separate Cloud setup.

The terminal package includes the plugin used by its own scans. You can follow
the CLI quick start without setting up an interactive
Codex plugin session.
## Choose a task
| Task | In Codex | From the terminal |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Scan a repository or selected paths | Ask for a Standard scan ($security-scan). | cs scan . or cs scan . --path src |
| Review a PR, commit, branch diff, or working-tree patch | Ask for $security-diff-scan with the change to review. | cs scan . --diff origin/main for committed changes, or cs scan . --working-tree for local changes. |
| Run repeated audits of the same target | Ask for $deep-security-scan. Later audits use findings from earlier ones. | cs scan . --mode deep |
| Assess supplied findings against the source | $triage-finding returns a verdict and any missing evidence for each claim. | cs validate findings.json returns a validation report. |
| Investigate a dependency alert | Give $resolve-dependency-alert the alert and the checkout or image. It traces the dependency and proposes an upgrade or dismissal where the evidence supports one. | To retrieve a saved alert for that review, see below. |
| Prepare a fix | Ask $fix-finding to patch a specific finding in the affected repository. | cs patch --scan SCANID |
| Check an existing fix | Give $verify-fix the finding and current checkout. | cs verify-fix --scan SCANID |
| Track a validated finding | Give $track-findings the finding and destination. See plugin connectors. | For completed scans, see publishing to Linear. |
| Inspect a downloaded skill | Review the skill before installation in a trusted Codex chat. | Use the interactive Codex CLI with the plugin enabled. |

Read a saved dependency alert. Run cs findings imported ./project --format json
to list th
## Review a skill before installation
To review a skill before giving it to a coding agent, ask
$check-skills directly:

> Use $check-skills on ../downloaded-skills before I install them in Claude Code.

Start the chat in a trusted workspace with the Codex Security checker enabled.
Keep the downloaded checkout outside the host's skill discovery paths and pass
its path to the checker. If you already opened the checkout as your workspace
or enabled its skills, start a clean chat with the target outside discovery.
The previous chat may have loaded its AGENTS.md or a replacement checker.

Point it at a file, an extracted bundle, a checkout containing several skills,
or paste the skill text. It returns a per-skill PASS, REVIEW, BLOCK,
or INCOMPLETE with source evidence and coverage limits. A file review covers
only that file. Supply the folder to include helpers and references. The review
does not install the target or require the plugin MCP server.

row.description: 紫微斗数开源排盘引擎 — 基于倪海厦《天纪》体系，含完整排盘算法、四化系统、格局知识库、古籍原文数据

markdown:
## 算法是公开的传统智慧，不应该被锁在围墙里
中文 · English

 

一、项目理念：紫微斗数是中国传统命理学的瑰宝，倪海厦老师在《天纪》中系统梳理了正宗的紫微斗数体系。我们希望通过技术手段让更多人接触和学习这门学问。

开源排盘算法和知识库，是因为我们相信：算法是公开的传统智慧，不应该被锁在围墙里。真正的价值在于解读的深度、用户体验的打磨、以及持续运营的积累。

二、项目信息：基于 倪海厦《天纪》 教学体系的紫微斗数排盘系统，包含完整排盘算法、四化系统、格局知识库、古籍原文数据，以及一套完整开源的紫微斗数解读数据：v4.0 解读数据集——67.5 万张命盘 × 13 维 = 877 万段解读，正文约 204 亿字，解压后 56.6 GB（2026-10-15 发布）。

| 数据集 | 命盘 | 解读段数 | 解压后 | 覆盖年份 | 每张盘解读字数 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v4.0 解读数据集（2026-10-15） | 674,976 | 8,774,688 | 56.6 GB | 1950–2026（只含真实日期） | 约 3.0 万字 |
| v3.0 样本数据集 | 518,400 | 6,739,200 | 33.1 GB | 1924–1983 | 约 2.1 万字 |
| 变化 | +30% | +30% | +71% | +17 年 | +44% |

 v3.0 每张盘解读字数按 2,160 张盘抽样估算，其余数字为全量统计；两版每张盘都是 13 维。 

在线体验：ouranic.cn，排盘、AI 解读、命盘历史全部开放。

> 注：关于六亲判断
>
> 紫微斗数在六亲（父母、兄弟、子女等）判断上存在一定局限。倪师在《天纪》中指出：“斗数批六亲本来就比较差一点。”（2上 · 00:25:27）在传统术数中，铁板神数在核对六亲方面有其独特优势（2上 · 00:03:15）；倪师仍以紫微斗数为核心，是因为它能结合地理、环境与人事进行综合判断，形成“上知天文、下知地理、中知人事”的完整体系（2上 · 00:25:43）。因此，与六亲相关的分析仅供参考；ouranic.cn 上父母、兄弟、子女三个维度也附有同样的说明。

## 一、本轮更新（2026-10-15）
本轮跟随网站 2026-10-15 发版（网站内容版本 ca268829f7a9）：



1. 发布 13 维解读数据集 v4.0 —— 674,976 张命盘（公历 1950–2026 年每一个真实日期 × 12 时辰 × 男女）× 13 维 = 8,774,688 段解读，正文约 204 亿字。解压后 56.6 GB（v3.0 为 33.1 GB，增加 71%），压缩后只有 161 MB，按年份分 77 个文件，可以只下需要的年份，也可以一次下全年份总包。下载见 Release v4.0-13d，规格和字段见第二·新章。发布前 77 个文件逐个解压，与原始数据逐字节比对一致。

2. 13 维断语按倪师原话与《全书》原文逐句校正（断语库仍不开源，校正结果体现在 v4.0 数据集里）：

- 标着倪师或《全书》却查不到出处的引文，删掉或换成逐字可查的原话；倪师原话注明《天纪》第几集、几分几秒
- 不会发生的四化（如七杀化权、紫微化忌）相关的句子删去；只在某种条件下才成立的断语补上条件

## Algorithms are openly shared traditional wisdom; they shouldn’t be locked behind walls.
中文 · English

 

1. Philosophy: Zi Wei Dou Shu is a treasure of traditional Chinese astrology, and Ni Haixia laid out its authentic system in Tian Ji (《天纪》). We hope technology can bring more people to learn it.

We open-source the charting algorithm and the knowledge base because we believe algorithms are openly shared traditional wisdom and shouldn’t be locked behind walls. The real value lies in the depth of interpretation, a carefully polished user experience, and what we build up by running the service day after day.

2. About the project: A Zi Wei Dou Shu (紫微斗数, "Purple Star Astrology") charting engine following the teaching system of Ni Haixia's Tian Ji (倪海厦《天纪》). It includes the full charting algorithm, the Four Transformations (四化), a pattern knowledge base, public-domain classical texts, and a 518,400-chart sample dataset, plus a 674,976-chart × 13-topic interpretation dataset (v4.0, 2026-10-15): 8.77 million readings, about 20.4 billion characters of text, 56.6 GB uncompressed — up from 518,400 charts and 33.1 GB in v3.0.

## What the engine handles
| Feature | Notes |
|---|---|
| True solar time | Longitude offset plus the equation of time, so births near hour boundaries are not off by one double-hour |
| China DST | 1986–1991 daylight-saving periods are detected (not subtracted automatically; convert the clock reading with clock-adjust.ts once the user confirms) |
| Leap months | Four configurable conventions (previous month / next month / split by day / same month) |
| Late Zi hour | 23:00–23:59 is charted on the next day, 00:00–00:59 on the same day; with a birthplace the cutoff uses true solar time (same as the hour branch); switchable |
| Star brightness | 7 levels (庙 旺 得 利 平 不 陷); brightness tables of different schools are switchable, not hard-coded |
| Four Transformations | Natal, decade (大限) and annual (流年) transformations, plus flying-star self-transformations |
| Twelve spirits | Natal layer by year branch, annual layer by the annual branch |
| Patterns | 1,100+ lines of pattern rules (紫府同宫, 日月并明, 七杀朝斗, …) |

Engine code lives in lib/ziwei/ (entry point: generateChart() in algorithm.ts). Inputs are a Gregorian date and an hour branch index 0–11 (子 = 0 … 亥 = 11), not a clock hour.
## Quick start
No API key is needed for charting. The open-source version contains no backend routes: AI interpretation (/api/interpret) and compatibility analysis (/api/heming) return 404 until you implement them yourself.
